research.facts:
F1 Calendar Crisis — Qatar and Abu Dhabi at Risk
**Facts (HIGH confidence — Sky Sports, Al Jazeera, RacingNews365, GPFans):**
- Bahrain GP and Saudi Arabian GP already officially cancelled in March 2026 — due to US-Iran war; US/Israel launched airstrikes on Iran; missile and drone attacks hit Gulf states
- Qatar GP scheduled: Nov 27-29, 2026
- Abu Dhabi GP scheduled: Dec 4-6, 2026
- F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali confirmed on July 29 that a mid-September 2026 deadline has been set to decide whether Qatar and Abu Dhabi can proceed
- Domenicali stated: "2026 season will definitively end in Europe if Middle East races cannot go ahead"
- Primary contingency for Qatar: Imola (Italy), on standby per RTE report
- Other contingencies: Turkey, Portugal, Hockenheim (Germany) for Abu Dhabi slot
- WEC (World Endurance Championship) has already confirmed it will not race in Middle East at year-end
- Domenicali acknowledged December European racing logistics (potential snow)
research.sources:
- Source: Sky Sports, Al Jazeera, RacingNews365, GPFans (all July 29 reports)
**Facts (MEDIUM confidence):**
- Brexit-related customs complications rule out non-European alternatives at short notice (per Domenicali; single source)
- Bahrain cancellation came in March 2026; exact announcement date not confirmed in all sources

research.facts:
Verstappen Contract Saga — Red Bull's Counter-Offer
**Facts (HIGH confidence — ESPN, PlanetF1, F1 Oversteer, The Judge13):**
- Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract runs through 2028 with performance-related exit clauses
- Exit clause can be triggered in October if Verstappen is NOT in top 2 in championship at summer break
- Verstappen currently 7th in standings — exit clause is triggerable (confirmed by ESPN, PlanetF1)
- Red Bull submitted new contract offer: approximately €65M (~$72M) per year through 2029
- Key condition of Red Bull's offer: removal of all exit clause language
- As of July 28: Verstappen has NOT responded to the offer (source: TheJudge13 July 28)
- Sport Bible (July 7): Verstappen and McLaren in "closing stages" of negotiations for 2027 move
- McLaren CEO Zak Brown publicly denies any Verstappen talks, reiterates commitment to Norris/Piastri
- Piastri/Red Bull swap rumor: Red Bull reportedly targeting Piastri, though Piastri locked in at McLaren until 2028+
- Verstappen's public stance: "There's nothing to say" when asked about future
- Lambiase (Verstappen's race engineer): reportedly in discussions with McLaren for 2028
**Facts (MEDIUM confidence):**
- McLaren "closing stages" report from Sport Bible (July 7) — McLaren denies
- Piastri swap rumor: single source, unconfirmed by parties

Aston Martin B-Spec Upgrade at Hungarian GP
**Facts (HIGH confidence — The Race, Autosport, F1.com, Motorsport.com):**
- Aston Martin debuted 16-part B-spec overhaul at Hungarian GP (July 24-26)
- Parts changed: front wing, front wing endplate, nose, front corner, floor body, floor corners, floor fences, floor edge, diffuser, sidepod inlet, engine cover, cooling louvres, rear suspension, rear corner, rear wing, beam wing, rear wing endplate
- Mechanics used team's first curfew exemption of 2026 season to complete overnight installation
- Primary goals: fix baseline aerodynamic efficiency and weight issues plaguing car all season
- Results: Fernando Alonso qualified in Q2 for FIRST TIME ALL SEASON (ending streak of back-row qualifications)
- Alonso quote (F1.com): "That adrenaline was missed" — "I could fight a little bit more"
- Alonso race result: 14th
- Lance Stroll: 13th
- This is explicitly step 1 of 2 — step 2 debuts at Dutch GP (Aug 21-23) along with Honda PU upgrade
- Alpine's Franco Colapinto issued "ominous warning" about upgraded Aston Martin's potential
**Facts (MEDIUM confidence):**
- Specific percentage gain numbers not confirmed (+2.036% quoted in one source but unverified against others)

research.facts:
Dutch GP at Zandvoort — Last Race, Sprint Debut
**Facts (HIGH confidence — World of Speed, Scuderia Fans, Dutch GP official, The Race):**
- Dutch GP dates: August 21-23, 2026 (Round 12 of 22)
- This is the LAST-EVER Formula 1 race at Circuit Zandvoort — F1 will not return after 2026
- Dutch GP 2026 is a SPRINT WEEKEND — first Sprint format ever held at Zandvoort
- Sprint weekend schedule:
- Friday: Sprint Qualifying 16:30 CET
- Saturday: Sprint Race 12:00 CET (24 laps, ~30 minutes)
- Saturday: GP Qualifying 16:00 CET
- Sunday: Main Race 15:00 CET (72 laps)
- Aston Martin second B-spec upgrade step debuts at Dutch GP
- Honda power unit upgrade debuts at Dutch GP
- Verstappen context: If he triggers exit clause in October, Dutch GP could be his last as a Red Bull driver racing at his home circuit
**Facts (MEDIUM confidence):**
- Commercial reasons for Zandvoort exit: VAT increase, economics, difficulty attracting top drivers (sold out but financially challenging)
- Zandvoort F1 history: circuit returned to calendar in 2021 (first Dutch GP since 1985)
